title: Optimal Large-Contest Design
abstract: arXiv:2601.19331v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: In this paper, we provide a theoretical framework to analyze the optimal design of large contests, such as university admissions and research funding. Under a broad class of distributional preferences, the optimal allocation rules are step functions with at most two steps, thus rationalizing several real-world examples. From a methodological perspective, we leverage the mathematics of extreme points to characterize optimal allocation rules in environments where the distribution of efforts can be endogenous. When the designer wants to maximize aggregate effort, the optimal allocation rule sets a performance threshold and it awards prizes at random above it, provided noise is sufficiently small. When noise is larger, awarding prizes to the best performers becomes optimal.

translated_abstract: 在本文中，我们提供了一个理论框架来分析大型竞赛（如大学录取和科研经费资助）的最优设计。在一类广泛的分布偏好下，最优分配规则是至多两级的阶梯函数，这为若干现实世界中的例子提供了理论依据。从方法论角度看，我们利用极值点的数学方法来刻画在努力分布可以内生化的环境中的最优分配规则。当设计者希望最大化总努力时，若噪声足够小，最优分配规则会设定一个绩效门槛，并在门槛之上随机分配奖品；当噪声较大时，将奖品授予表现最好的参与者则成为最优选择。
tldr: 本文提出了大型竞赛最优设计的理论框架，证明最优分配规则是至多两级的阶梯函数：噪声较小时应在绩效门槛之上随机分配奖品，噪声较大时则应奖励表现最好的参与者。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for optimal large-contest design, showing that optimal allocation rules are step functions with at most two steps: when noise is small, prizes should be awarded randomly above a performance threshold, while with larger noise, rewarding the best performers becomes optimal.
